faqs.question: What can I study in the March intake?
faqs.answer: Spring options include Chinese language and foundation programmes. Some pathways prepare you for a later bachelor degree. Direct bachelor and master entry depend on the university and programme; your shortlist will identify the correct degree start term.

faqs.question: Do I need IELTS, HSK or CSCA?
faqs.answer: Requirements depend on the course and teaching language. Chinese-medium routes may require HSK; English-medium degrees require accepted English evidence. NUAA foundation does not require a CSCA score for entry, but degree progression requires a satisfactory score. Your selected programme determines the full requirements.

faqs.question: Does a scholarship cover every expense?
faqs.answer: Tuition, accommodation, insurance and stipend are separate award components. Your written scholarship award determines coverage, conditions and renewal. We only deduct supported reductions in your ClearCost plan.

faqs.question: Which documents do I need?
faqs.answer: Start with your passport, academic certificates and transcripts. Language evidence, health examination, police clearance and financial evidence depend on the programme. Postgraduate applicants may also need a study plan and recommendation letters. Documents are required for both self-funded and scholarship applications.

faqs.question: What happens after I request a study plan?
faqs.answer: An EduExpress counsellor reviews your qualification, result and programme interest, then contacts you about a shortlist, scholarship eligibility, a written cost breakdown and a document checklist. File processing begins after you agree on the programme and service terms.

faqs.question: Can my parents join the consultation?
faqs.answer: Yes. You and your family can discuss programme fit, costs, payment terms and document preparation by phone or at our Dhanmondi office.
